Pretraining Dynamics: we pretrain a series of autoregressive transformer-based models using unlabeled DNA data, with log-uniformly spaced sizes ranging from 20 Million to 1 Billion.
We utilize the Hugging Face Trainer API for full-size fine-tuning of the pretrained checkpoints.

evidence.quote: The success of LLMs is pretraining transformer-based autoregressive models (Vaswani, 2017) on internet-scale data, followed by post-training to increase instruction-following abilities (Lambert et al., 2024). Inspired by this, we ask: is it possible to develop a generalist genomic foundation model for addressing diverse genomic tasks simultaneously?

representation_rationale.summary: The authors motivate an autoregressive transformer strategy by the success of LLM pretraining and post-training.

evidence.quote: The pretrained model needs to be separately finetuned K times given K tasks. This results in the additional cost of storing O ( K ) copies of model weights, incurring significant I/O latency, memory costs, and context-switching penalties.

representation_rationale.summary: A unified multi-task model avoids repeated task-specific fine-tuning, duplicated weights, and context switching.

evidence.quote: The output space of existing models is rigidly constrained to DNA sequences or predefined genomic labels, limiting their ability to generate diverse, semantically meaningful outputs.

representation_rationale.summary: The authors argue that existing rigid output formats limit text and image generation from DNA.

evidence.quote: To alleviate it, we should minimize the size of added tokens.

representation_rationale.summary: Vocabulary expansion shifts probabilities of existing tokens, so the authors identify minimizing added-token vocabulary as important.

evidence.quote: achieving high-fidelity cross-modality translation remains an open challenge.

representation_rationale.summary: The authors identify high-fidelity cross-modal translation as an unresolved limitation.
